# Shared Blender execution guidance

Use this guidance once when a task needs a BAS specialist. Select the durable
source and required outputs through the shared
[source and delivery contract](../../../../../references/source-delivery.md).
Specialists add domain checks within that contract. A local repair revisits the
affected work and its preservation constraints; it does not reopen every stage
of a previously accepted asset.

## References and construction

For a new recognizable subject or substantial shape repair, inspect the user's
references before detailed construction. Fill a consequential missing angle or
feature with available image search or browser tools. Search by the question
being answered: front for spacing, profile for depth, and close views for joints
or identifying details. Reuse accepted references for small edits.

Keep observations separate from inferred hidden geometry. Label analogues from
different subjects or product variants; do not combine them into an invented
turnaround. Record the source, useful view, observed relationship, and uncertainty
beside the project. Inspect actual images before claiming comparison. Stop
gathering references when the modeling questions have enough coverage; state any
remaining gaps. Viewing a reference does not grant rights to redistribute it as
a texture or published asset.

Connect the brief to concrete relationships before surface detail: dimensions,
proportions, negative spaces, supports, pivots, contacts, material boundaries,
and motion states. Choose construction that satisfies them together. Compare
matching graybox views before polishing. Use complementary views when depth or
attachment is ambiguous. Preserve requested stylization and accepted parts.

Keep the task's quality milestones observable. Adjacent stages may share a
build and evidence pass. An interior-only or render-only task does not require
unseen exterior construction; a whole-asset handoff needs its promised coverage.
For characters, use the character workflow's form and deformation checks where
the current work affects anatomy, fit, or articulation.

## Evidence that informs the next edit

After a coherent edit, inspect relevant numeric constraints and low-cost views.
Tie each visible defect to a view or frame and the source-level cause best
supported by that evidence. Mark ambiguous relationships as unresolved instead
of assigning unsupported passes. Open individual images when a contact sheet
cannot establish a joint, seam, or material detail.

For a full asset presentation, prepare a readable hero image and the contracted
diagnostic views. Adapt lighting after inspecting the image and preserve the
user's art direction. Authored scene lighting is appropriate for final renders;
standard evidence lighting serves geometry checks. For local repairs, compare
the affected views and critical neighboring poses under unchanged settings.

Run fresh export/import checks when a requested downstream asset format is
affected by the edit. For native scenes, reopen the source and resolve its
dependencies in a clean Blender process. For scripted sources, rerun the
generator or recorded patch against its declared baseline. Inspect actual final
images or continuous motion when the requested behavior cannot be established
by still frames. A successful process, metric, or sparse sample does not prove
visual fidelity or continuous collision freedom.

Keep useful source snapshots, baseline evidence, and the exact checks applied.
Once the applicable checks pass, deliver. Repeat checks for new changes,
failures, or unresolved concerns. A successful local repair can retain unrelated
pre-existing defects, which must remain disclosed and outside claims of repair.
Declared preservation invariants must still hold.

## Continuity and execution

For long work, keep a compact checkpoint beside the source: requested outcome,
accepted decisions, source revision, evidence paths, known defects, pending
jobs, and next action. On resume, verify files and job state before continuing.
When the user changes direction, invalidate only affected evidence or caches.

Use frozen inputs and separate output directories when overlapping independent
jobs. Do not edit an asset or cache while a running job consumes it. The local
MCP serializes its own jobs; separate Blender processes still need coordinated
GPU usage. Record execution failures separately from completed checks that
found defects.

Model choice, delegation, permissions, and host tools follow the user's request
and the current host instructions. This domain guide supplies no model override
or mandatory extra approval step. Benchmark methodology is loaded only for an
explicit comparison task through the benchmark specialist.
